classification: Diagnostic delivery repair; not a calendar or website latency repair

original.finding: Original calendar lookup lost its session; LLDB launch/stack collection and screenshot capture were terminated without retained native thread evidence. All original diagnostics remain preserved.

question: Can the operating system sampler retain the original pinned process's native thread report under the existing 10-second command and 15-second handoff limits when debugger startup is unavailable?

method.healthyPath: Unchanged: passive device log identity and existing frame observation only; no native sampler or process inspection before an actual failed scenario.
method.failedPath: Keep independent screenshot capture. Inspect only the pinned PID through kernel metadata before and after the one-second native sample. Both checks must retain the same full owned executable and kernel launch timestamp. Validate the report's exact PID and native call graph. An exact executable path or a single whole-component privacy mask consistent with that full kernel path is accepted; unbounded, partial-component, multiple or mismatching masks fail. Preserve raw output, both kernel rows, identity proof and errors.
method.budgets: Each kernel inspection 5000 ms; screenshot 5000 ms; native stack collector 10000 ms; all operations share the original handoff deadline at most 15000 ms. The second inspection is one bounded attribution check, not polling or a retry. No deadline, retry, sleep, polling, workload or watchdog increase.
method.controls: Recorded debugger-start failure regression; exact raw macOS 27 privacy-redacted report replay; reused PID/same path/different launch rejection; exited, other-device and missing-launch rejection; wrong PID/path and empty report rejection; original ownership/deadline/handoff regressions; a real disposable native process control on macOS, with no CoreSimulator RPC or app launch. Its intentionally unavailable screenshot must still fail the diagnostic result.

completedAllocation.head: 26de8b4d08a0f69637e1e4adab2586e183a10d24
completedAllocation.finding: Both actual macOS native controls retained real native thread samples within the cap. The validator rejected the operating system's privacy-redacted temporary executable path, and an unsafe frame-error assertion hid that diagnostic result. Neither iOS scenario suite started. This allocation is exhausted, not a passing collector or calendar acceptance.
completedAllocation.preservation: All 13 complete diagnostic/report/coverage archives and nine job logs retained with archive and 234 decoded-entry SHA256 hashes. Two large app binaries are metadata/digest-only. Both original raw native reports and errors are retained.

allocation: One automatic normal CI workflow on the concrete corrective head, after local red/green replay of the actual macOS report and process-instance rejection tests. No additional unchanged allocation on the exhausted head. Inspect every actual macOS control result and original mobile outcome; preserve complete reports, archives and logs before any further push.
stop: Stop after the corrective head's one complete workflow, whether it passes or fails. No unchanged manual rerun or merging solely to create another measurement. A healthy control or non-reproducing calendar run does not explain or erase the original stall. This correction only addresses the observed report-attribution defect; a genuine stalled app may still defeat collection.
unchanged: Application source and appearance, accessible content, interaction deadlines, mobile recovery policy, all reader scenarios/controls/legacy guard, and seven separate panel quarantines. No Store or AWS mutations.
